properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepted on input in national or
            international form (spaces, dashes and brackets allowed); stored and returned
            in canonical E.164 form, e.g. '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^\+?[0-9 ()\-]*$'
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted, and is returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID

## Summary

The rule: reject creating an owner when another owner has the same `lastName` **and** the same `address` (compared case-insensitively, whitespace collapsed) → **409**, unless the request sets `sharesHousehold: true`.

I followed the existing `EnsureUniqueTelephone` pattern rather than inventing a new shape, so the new logic sits in one small step alongside its peers.

**Changes:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a `sharesHousehold` boolean to the `OwnerFields` schema (marked `writeOnly`, not required). This regenerates `OwnerFieldsDto` with a `getSharesHousehold()` accessor so the opt-in flag can be read from the request body without a second `@RequestBody` binding.

2. **`EnsureUniqueHousehold.java`** (new step) — skips the check when `sharesHousehold` is true; otherwise normalizes `lastName` and `address` (trim, collapse internal whitespace to a single space, lower-case via `Locale.ROOT`) and scans existing owners for a match, throwing `DuplicateHouseholdException` on a hit. Normalization lives in one private helper so both fields are compared identically.

3. **`DuplicateHouseholdException.java`** — a checked exception (mirrors `DuplicateTelephoneException`).

4. **`DuplicateHouseholdExceptionHandler.java`** + **escalation YAML** — maps the exception to a 409 `ProblemDetail`, reusing the shared `ProblemDetails.build(...)` helper.

5. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted the `ensureHousehold` step (under the `transaction` governance) between the telephone-uniqueness check and `build`.

**Verification:** All three new acceptance tests pass — reject on same lastName+address (409), allow with a different address, and allow when `sharesHousehold: true` — and the full suite is `BUILD SUCCESS`.

One note: because the `spring` openapi-generator applies `writeOnly` only to the `@Schema` documentation and not to Jackson's `@JsonProperty`, `sharesHousehold` will serialize as `null` in `OwnerDto` responses. It's harmless to tests and semantically documented as write-only, but if you'd prefer it fully absent from responses that would require a generator-level `@JsonInclude(NON_NULL)` tweak. Let me know if you want that.
